rule: EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation for PFAS (final rule April 10, 2024)

compliance_determination.note: EPA determines MCL compliance using the running annual average at the sampling point. A single sample above an MCL is NOT by itself a violation. This application therefore reports a single high sample as 'above the benchmark' and only reports a compliance-relevant exceedance when a running annual average of four or more quarters meets or exceeds the MCL.

regulatory_status.summary: The April 2024 PFAS NPDWR remains in force as written. On May 18, 2026 EPA proposed two rules that would change it. Neither proposal is final, and a proposal does not change the current legal limits.

proposals.effect: Would rescind the regulatory determinations and MCLs for PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and the Hazard Index mixture of these three plus PFBS.
Would extend the PFOA and PFOS MCL compliance deadline from April 2029 to April 2031 via a federal exemption framework. The 4 ng/L MCLs themselves would be retained.

litigation.court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

events.event: Court denied EPA's request to summarily vacate the MCLs for PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA, and mixtures with PFBS.
Court denied EPA's motion to sever and stay challenges to those MCLs.

monitoring_deadline.note: All community and non-transient non-community water systems must complete initial PFAS monitoring by April 26, 2027. Florida DEP states the May 2026 proposals did not indicate this requirement would be revised or extended.

regulatory_status.enforcement_note: Florida DEP provides technical assistance and manages PFAS records on EPA's behalf; EPA conducts formal enforcement.

hazard_index.note: Hazard Index = sum of (measured / health-based concentration) across the four listed analytes. HI at or above 1.0 is an exceedance.

1,4-Dioxane.note: 1,4-dioxane has no federal enforceable MCL. 0.35 ug/L is the health advisory / cleanup target level referenced by Florida and EPA and used by Seminole County as an action level. A result above it is an action-level exceedance, not a regulatory violation.
